independent.summary: The new `failedUrls` are only persisted when a ScrapeSnapshot exists: `createSnapshot` returns null when there are no archivable chunks, so a first-ever full scrape (the signup path, and the case where knowing the unlearned URLs matters most) and a rescrape in which nothing changed both drop the list — it survives only in the transient socket summary, so the item's "persist it on the run's ScrapeSnapshot" holds only for re-scrapes of an already-populated entity.

A page classified `empty_after_render` is still pushed into `allPageData` (scraper.js:898), so it is counted in `pagesScraped` and gets a ScrapedPage row written by the final bulkWrite — the owner-facing headline count still includes pages simultaneously listed under "Not learned" (e.g. the test's 4-URL site reports 4 pages scraped with 1 of them unlearned).

The .env.example addition is a non-sensitive log-verbosity knob (SCRAPE_FAILURE_LOG_LEVEL); no credential, key, or secret handling is touched anywhere in the change.
No billing, Stripe, quota, or pricing code is in the diff.
The deleteMany/snapshot-restore logic is untouched — the diff only captures the snapshot's return value and adds an additive updateOne on a new field.
Outbound fetch behaviour (axios options, retries, Puppeteer trigger) is unchanged; the new module only classifies errors already being caught.
No deploy/build config or version change, and the new ScrapeSnapshot field is optional and additive, so no migration or release step is implicated.
